paragraphs: The whistle came first, then the grass. Yellow Duck Sweater had never stood on grass. It was wet, and it gave under each orange foot like unfinished carpet. Around the pitch rose eighty-two thousand green seats, every one folded up. A gold coin spun for the toss, landed on its edge, and rolled away between the tall white posts, which seemed lucky. Then the ball arrived. It was pointed at both ends, and it wobbled to a stop against the duck's toes. Egg, thought the duck. Nobody had trained it for an egg.

Three reference ducks came thumping down the pitch, plain white, heads low. The duck had no arms, but it did own a sweater slightly too big. It crouched and nudged the egg up under the hem until the knitted duckling bulged. Then it ran. This was only the hallway, painted with stripes. The reference ducks leaned on it, neck against neck, a slow warm shove. The duck leaned back and kept walking, and the whole knot of them slid over the white line and tipped into a heap. Every seat flapped down at once, like applause. The duck stayed where it had landed, sitting on the egg to keep it warm, while a moon with one side worn off hung between the posts.
text:
The whistle came first, then the grass. Yellow Duck Sweater had never stood on grass. It was wet, and it gave under each orange foot like unfinished carpet. Around the pitch rose eighty-two thousand green seats, every one folded up. A gold coin spun for the toss, landed on its edge, and rolled away between the tall white posts, which seemed lucky. Then the ball arrived. It was pointed at both ends, and it wobbled to a stop against the duck's toes. Egg, thought the duck. Nobody had trained it for an egg.

Three reference ducks came thumping down the pitch, plain white, heads low. The duck had no arms, but it did own a sweater slightly too big. It crouched and nudged the egg up under the hem until the knitted duckling bulged. Then it ran. This was only the hallway, painted with stripes. The reference ducks leaned on it, neck against neck, a slow warm shove. The duck leaned back and kept walking, and the whole knot of them slid over the white line and tipped into a heap. Every seat flapped down at once, like applause. The duck stayed where it had landed, sitting on the egg to keep it warm, while a moon with one side worn off hung between the posts.
imagePrompt: Yellow Duck Sweater, a small two-legged tabletop robot. Its head is a smooth, chunky white plastic shell shaped like a small loaf of bread: about one and a half times as long front to back as it is tall, deep and boxy with softly rounded corners and a mostly flat top. It is not a round dome or ball, and not a long thin tube. It has an orange trim along the bottom edge and a small orange hinge on each side. At the front of the head is a single round camera eye: a black lens inside a thick orange-yellow ring. It has no beak and no mouth. The head sits on a tall, thin neck, about as tall as the head is long, made of stacked black servo motors with a few loose black wires, leaning slightly forward. Its body is a small, boxy white torso with rounded corners. It has no arms and no hands. Its short legs are black servo joints with white plastic covers on the hips, knees slightly bent. Its feet are flat and rounded like duck feet, orange on top with yellow soles. It wears a small, chunky-knit, bright lemon-yellow crewneck sweater over its white torso, slightly too big, with a ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem. Knitted into the front of the sweater is a simple cartoon duckling: pale yellow body with a thick black outline, a black dot eye, a curved line for its wing, an orange beak, and orange feet. A single full-color comic page with six panels of equal size in a grid of two columns and three rows, separated by clean white gutters, read left to right and top to bottom. The same robot duck appears in every panel and looks identical each time, unless a panel says otherwise. No speech bubbles, captions, sound effects, panel numbers, or any other text. Panel 1: The duck stands alone on the wet, striped grass of a huge empty rugby stadium at night under a cloudy sky, with tiers of folded-up green seats rising all around and tall white H-shaped goalposts behind it. Panel 2: The duck tilts its head to watch a large gold coin roll away on its edge across the grass and between the two tall white goalposts. Panel 3: The duck bends its neck to look down at an oval rugby ball, pointed at both ends, resting on the grass against its orange toes. Panel 4: Four ducks: the duck in the yellow sweater crouches over the oval ball and nudges it up under the hem of its sweater, while far down the pitch three robot ducks with no sweaters, plain white, run toward it side by side. Panel 5: Four ducks: the duck in the yellow sweater, with a big oval bulge under its sweater stretching the knitted duckling, leans forward neck to neck against the three sweaterless white ducks, and all four slide together across the grass toward a white line. Panel 6: The duck sits alone on top of the oval ball like a bird on an egg, on the grass just past the white line, with every green stadium seat now folded down and a lopsided, nearly full moon hanging between the tall white goalposts as the clouds part. Warm children's comic art: clean confident ink outlines, soft flat colors with gentle shading, a dreamy night palette, cozy and a little surreal. Friendly for an 11-year-old. No text, letters, logos, or numbers anywhere in the image. Real people do not appear.
